title: An Iranian canal drove mills through rock-cut tunnels
body: At Shushtar, engineers diverted water from Iran's Karun River into two main canals. The Gargar canal sends water through a system of tunnels that historically drove mills before the water dropped into a basin.
takeaway: A single diversion can deliver water and provide the energy to grind grain.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Shushtar Historical Hydraulic System (2009)
visual: water pouring from tunnel mouths into a stone basin at Shushtar

title: Lamu's old houses were built with coral stone and mangrove wood
body: In Kenya's island town of Lamu, builders used coral stone for walls and mangrove timber for structural elements. Courtyards, verandas and elaborately carved wooden doors are features of the old town's buildings.
takeaway: The choice of materials shows how coastal environments shape local building traditions.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Lamu Old Town
visual: a carved wooden door set in a coral-stone wall on a narrow lane in Lamu
